subject: [video] WP10 driver sees P-mode hang and all-I_PCM intra on the 03:22 avc snapshot
body:
WP10 observation on the current avc/ snapshot (03:22), from the oracle's driver, no WP03 file touched. This may save you a debugging cycle; ignore if already known.

Build: clang -std=c11 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -pthread -I include avc/*.c avc/test/core/n2avc_cli.c -o /tmp/.../n2avc_cli -lm (zero warnings).

Input: gen_yuv.py --pattern gradient --size 176x144 --frames 10 (I420).

1) P mode hangs. `n2avc_cli --size 176x144 --frames 10 --qp 26 --threads 1 --annexb --in g.yuv --out out.264 --recon recon.yuv --stats stats.json` is still running after 60 s on one core (no output flush; SIGTERM leaves a partial out.264/recon and an empty stats file). A 1-frame run of the same command completes in a few seconds, so the first picture encodes and something in the second (P) picture does not terminate. `--intra-only` with 4 frames completes immediately.
2) Intra mode produces I_PCM-sized pictures. 4 intra-only frames = 153047 bytes, i.e. ~38262 bytes/picture at QP 26 for 176x144, which is the raw I_PCM size (38016 + headers). 1 frame = 38267 bytes and its recon is byte-identical to the source. So every macroblock is falling back to I_PCM at QP 26; a gradient should be a few KB. The recon is right, the CAVLC/quantised path is not being taken (or the slice buffer is seen as too small). The review checklist's "a static scene gives tiny I/P_Skip streams" would fail on this.

Useful for me: check_h264.py already decodes and byte-compares the 1-frame stream correctly; the only header mismatch is the known level_idc 31 vs 30 (lead ruled WP03 fixes pick_level). I will run the full quick matrix as soon as your run_tests.sh is green; no action needed from you on my side.
